result_expr: Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*rho_v(x, y, z, t), t) + Derivative(rho_i(T(x, y, z, t))*phi(x, y, z, t), t) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), x), x) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y), y) - Derivative((1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*D_v(T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), z), z)

symbols.name: rho_i(T)
symbols.meaning: density of ice (mass of water per unit volume of ice)

symbols.name: D_v(T)
symbols.meaning: diffusivity of water vapor in the pore gas

symbols.name: m
symbols.meaning: total water mass (ice plus vapor) per unit total volume

symbols.name: J
symbols.meaning: vapor mass flux per unit total area

symbols.name: V
symbols.meaning: fixed control volume in the pore space, with boundary \partial V and outward unit normal \mathbf{n}

symbols.name: R
symbols.meaning: residual of the water mass balance

steps.title: Integral water mass balance
steps.why: Water is neither created nor destroyed; it only changes phase. So the water mass in a fixed control volume $V$ changes only by the flux $\mathbf{J}$ through its boundary.
steps.operation: conservation of mass for a fixed control volume

check.printed: Statement of the conservation principle; no tool check.

steps.title: Water mass per unit total volume
steps.why: A fraction $\phi$ of each volume is ice with density $\rho_i$, and a fraction $1-\phi$ is gas carrying vapor at density $\rho_v$ per unit gas volume. Both phases hold water, so both enter $m$; this is where the ice-vapor exchange is accounted for.
steps.operation: volume-fraction weighting of the phase densities

check.printed: S2 m at phi=1: rho_i(T(x, y, z, t))  at phi=0: rho_v(x, y, z, t)

steps.title: Vapor flux
steps.why: Ice is rigid and does not move, so it carries no flux. Vapor moves by Fickian diffusion in the gas only; the flux per unit total area is weighted by the gas fraction $1-\phi$, which makes it vanish inside ice.
steps.operation: Fick's law applied to the gas fraction

check.printed: units div((1-phi) D grad rho_v) kilogram / meter ** 3 / second

steps.title: Local balance
steps.why: Apply the divergence theorem to the surface integral of S1; since $V$ is arbitrary and the fields are smooth (A1), the integrand must vanish pointwise. Substituting S2 and S3 gives the residual.
steps.operation: divergence theorem, arbitrary V, substitution of S2 and S3

check.printed: S4 local form minus R: 0; units of all three terms: kilogram / meter ** 3 / second

steps.title: Expanded form with constant ice density (optional)
steps.why: Only if $\rho_i$ is taken constant, the product rule shows the familiar form: the exchange term $(\rho_i-\rho_v)\partial_t\phi$ is the source of vapor from sublimation ($\partial_t\phi<0$). This step is a rewriting for the reader; the result keeps $\rho_i(T)$ general.
steps.operation: product rule on the time derivatives, with constant $\rho_i$

steps.title: Cartesian form
steps.why: Write the divergence and gradient of S4 in 3D Cartesian coordinates to give the requested residual.

check.printed: R printed in expanded Cartesian form; local form minus R: 0

assumptions_used: A1: $\phi(x,y,z,t)$ and $T(x,y,z,t)$ are known, smooth fields (given).
A2: Water mass is conserved; it changes phase between ice and vapor but has no other sources or sinks (no chemical binding to regolith, no adsorption).
A3: The ice is a rigid, immobile solid with density $\rho_i(T)$ (no ice velocity, no deformation or sintering flow).
A4: Vapor is transported only by Fickian diffusion in the gas fraction with diffusivity $D_v(T)$; the gas has no bulk (advective) velocity.
A5: The effective diffusive flux in the diffuse interface is weighted by the gas fraction $1-\phi$, so no vapor flux passes through ice.

neglected.effect: Advection of vapor by bulk gas flow, including Stefan flow caused by sublimation
neglected.why: The Stefan velocity is about $\rho_v/\rho_{gas}$ times the diffusive velocity. Near 200 K, $\rho_v \sim 10^{-5}$ kg m$^{-3}$, which is small, and no imposed pressure gradient drives flow in the pores.

neglected.effect: Thermal diffusion (Soret effect) and pressure diffusion
neglected.why: The Soret coefficient for water vapor in air is of order 0.01-0.1 of the Fick flux per relative temperature change; with pore-scale $\Delta T/T \ll 1$ it is a small correction.

neglected.effect: Knudsen or transition-regime transport in near-vacuum lunar pores
neglected.why: This is not strictly neglected: it changes the value and the dependence of $D_v$, which can depend on pore size as well as $T$. The form of the balance stays the same, but $D_v$ must be chosen for the gas-pressure regime.

neglected.effect: Vapor adsorption on regolith grain surfaces and surface diffusion
neglected.why: The work order defines only ice and gas in the pore space, so grains are outside the domain; adsorbed water would need its own balance.

neglected.effect: Ice motion (creep, sintering flow) and density change with temperature
neglected.why: Ice velocities are negligible on the time scales of sublimation. The thermal expansion of ice is about $10^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$; $\rho_i(T)$ is kept in the result anyway, and it can be set constant.

neglected.effect: Anisotropy or tortuosity of diffusion in the diffuse interface beyond the $(1-\phi)$ weighting
neglected.why: These affect only the interface layer, which is thin compared with the pore size, so the error is of the order of the interface width over the pore size.
